name: agent-chat
title: Agent Chat
description: The Blocks agent chat surface: full conversation UI for app agents (streaming markdown, tool cards, human-in-the-loop choice prompts, inline dynamic chat components, attachments) over the platform chat runtime (@blocksdiy/react-common/new-agent-chat — CopilotKit/AG-UI under the hood). ALWAYS use this for agent/AI chat pages wired to useAgentChat — never hand-build agent chat UI and never compose it from generic chat/message primitives. Ships the FLOATING AGENT CHAT too: a conversation with an agent in a panel over the page, opened from any page (the blocks-client skill → agents.md).
docs: Import { AgentChatSimple } from '@/components/ui/agent-chat' and render it inside a container with overflow-hidden AND a defined height (or inside <AgentViewport> from the agent-layout item, which fills to the viewport bottom by itself), passing agentChat from useAgentChat(<Name>AgentChat) (@blocksdiy/blocks-client-sdk/reactSdk, handle from @/product-types). Optional: size, defaultThreadId (a stable UUID per conversation, e.g. one chat per record — legacyChatThreadId(key) from @blocksdiy/react-common/agent-threads derives one from a string key; without it a signed-in user resumes their own latest conversation and an anonymous visitor gets a new one each mount; every chat of the same agent shares the same conversations), chatContext, placeholder, suggestions (starter prompts for a conversation with no messages yet — turns on the built-in welcome: agent avatar + greeting + chips, each sending as the first message; real prompts for this app, never placeholder copy), emptyState (your own hero instead), focusRunId (open the conversation at one agent run — the agentRunId a row the agent wrote carries). Use useAgent for the identity around the chat (header avatar/title). Every agent runs on this one chat, whatever its harness. An agent MINI-APP (an app.json miniApps item with `agent`) is not a lone chat — build its folder with the agent-layout item per the agent-mini-apps skill. FLOATING AGENT CHAT (floating-agent-chat.tsx, in this item): talk to an agent from a page without leaving it — useFloatingAgentChat().open({ agentChat, target?, expandHref?, newChatHref?, chatContext? }) under FloatingAgentChatProvider, mounted once in the layout that wraps the whole app; never a second panel. Every turn in it carries `urlContext` — the page's route params and search params (a repeated key as an array) — beside chatContext: the provider's `chatContext` (the app's, for every floating conversation) under the opener's — plus what the page itself tells the agent: `onScreen` (the table and query of every mounted entity read, built in) and useAgentContext(name, context) from @blocksdiy/blocks-client-sdk/reactSdk (a component's own state, under its name). Recipe: the blocks-client skill → agents.md. THE PLATFORM'S RAIL: the provider's `agents` ({ agent: <Name>Agent, agentChat: <Name>ChatAgentChat, entryRoute }, one per agent mini-app) is who the chat bubble on an agent's rail row can talk to — it opens a new chat with that agent in the floating chat panel, expanding to the mini-app's new-chat page. floating-agent-prompt.tsx (in this item) is retired: nothing opens it; don't build on it.

changelog.description: The config-change approval card (Remember this rule?) shows the agent's one- or two-sentence summary of the change with Approve and Reject, and the full change under a collapsed Show details; the rule text can no longer be edited on the card.

One chat for every agent: agent-chat.tsx is the chat itself (what deep-agent-chat.tsx was), its helpers are agent-chat-*.tsx (what deep-agent-chat-*.tsx were), and the deep-agent and react-agent chats are retired — the react-agent chat with its tool card and voice waveform. The platform runs every agent on it — a react agent, or one with no harness recorded, with its agent-chat block's instructions, tools and model settings, as configured. The react-agent chat is gone for good: an app that showed the two chat interfaces side by side now shows one, and nothing can bring the other back, so never offer to.
changelog.migration: The files listed as retired below are the old chat: deep-agent-chat.tsx is now agent-chat.tsx and each deep-agent-chat-<name> helper is now agent-chat-<name> — once the new files are in place, carry the app's own changes of each old one marked edited or without a version line into its new file, delete them all together with react-agent-chat.tsx, and point every '@/components/ui/deep-agent-chat' import at '@/components/ui/agent-chat' (and '@/components/ui/deep-agent-chat-<name>' at '@/components/ui/agent-chat-<name>'). Before touching agent-chat-tool-card.tsx and live-waveform.tsx, grep the app's own code for imports of them: keep an imported one exactly as it is, as the app's own file (it still works), and delete the rest. Then pnpm type-check finds what was written against the react-agent chat: remove variant and userPosition from AgentChatSimple; useAgentChat() now returns the deep-agent context — messages are AG-UI messages (role 'user' | 'assistant' | 'tool', content a string or parts; no msg, createdAt, 'human' or 'ai'), sendMessage({ content }) takes no hiddenContent, and threadIds, setThreadIds, addMessages, agentChatData, appId, token, agentChatId, chatId and noPersistency are gone (read agent and agentChat); AgentChatMessage takes { messageId } instead of { message, index }; AgentChatPrimitive is @blocksdiy/react-common/new-agent-chat, without ToolCard or voice primitives; withVoice has no effect and hideAttachmentButton is gone (attachments follow the agent-chat block's disableAttachments) — remove both; defaultThreadId must be a UUID — legacyChatThreadId(key) from @blocksdiy/react-common/agent-threads for a record key. A conversation held in the react-agent chat before this update, whatever its agent, does not show in the chat, which opens on the agent's greeting.

changelog.description: The send button becomes a Stop button (square icon, screen-reader label "Stop") while a reply Stop applies to is running: one sent from this chat, or one another tab's chat started. Stop ends the reply on the server and keeps what the agent had written so far, marked "Stopped" under the reply. Where the platform doesn't support it, the button is unchanged. No app code changes needed.
A turn a fired reminder or schedule started shows a step above the reply, styled like the tool steps: Reminder (or Scheduled) and its title.

Entries in the provider's agents carry the agent's full-page new chat, so a new chat that the platform's app rail (or openPrompt) opens in the panel shows the expand button before the first message; the expand leaves the page it came from in the route's history state, where agent-layout's minimize goes back to. The composer takes focus on every open, a repeated one included. With panel={null} the rail falls back to the agent's new-chat page and useFloatingAgentChatOptional returns null. The one-line floating prompt (floating-agent-prompt.tsx) is retired: it stays installed, unused; don't build on it.

Conversations are named by thread id alone: the chatId prop is deprecated (a chatId still opens the thread derived from it); with no thread, a signed-in user resumes their latest thread and an anonymous visitor starts a new one. The floating chat's target is { chatThreadId }.
Tool cards of long-running tools show 'Running in background' until the task's result arrives (task_status activity messages).

The floating agent chat now tells the agent what the page shows: the table and query of every mounted entity read (onScreen), and what components share with useAgentContext under their names. Its expand also shows on a new chat before the first send: it goes to the full-page new chat the opener passes to `open(…)` as `newChatHref` (the agent-layout's sidebar passes it). A page that opens the floating chat itself with `expandHref` should pass `newChatHref: newChatHref('<the agent mini-app route>')` from agent-layout-context too.
Brings the app's copy up to date and adds its version line.
